description:
Found by an s423 (#418) review probe; PRE-EXISTING (identical at a2ac578 and on
the s423 branch) and ASCII-only, so outside #418.  It is a MEASUREMENT trap,
not a PCL semantic bug: the generated CL is correct.

    print "a\n";
    for my $i (1..2) { }
    # perl:   "a\n"
    # runpcl: "a\n\n"

Loading the SAME emitted .lisp directly under sbcl gives "a\n" â the extra
newline is added by ./runpcl.  runpcl runs sbcl with `2>&1`, then strips
`;`-comment lines, the PCL banner and STYLE-WARNING lines, and finally
LEADING blank lines only (`s/\A(?:\s*\n)+//`, deliberately narrow since s386,
when a blanket strip deleted blank lines the PROGRAM printed).  cl/pcl-runtime.lisp
compiles with one style-warning block (undefined function %pcl-invert-case,
forward-referenced in %p-sub-perl-name), whose blank separator line survives
the `;` strip; with 2>&1 interleaving it can land AFTER the program output
instead of before it, where the leading-only strip cannot reach it.

Why it matters: every probe that byte-compares `./runpcl prog.pl` against
`perl prog.pl` can report a spurious DIFF (s423 probe p10 did).  The Pl/t
harness helper run_bytes is immune (it strips blank lines itself); run_file_bytes
is not.

Fix candidates, in order of cheapness:
  (a) run sbcl with stderr SEPARATE (capture 2> to a file, filter it, and
      forward only PCL:/real error lines) instead of 2>&1 â removes the
      interleaving entirely and is what the #339 drop-announcement path
      already does for the transpile side;
  (b) make the runtime compile without that style warning (declaim ftype or
      move %pcl-invert-case above %p-sub-perl-name) â removes this instance
      but not the class.
(a) is the real fix.  Add the two-line reproducer as a Pl/t row asserting a
byte-exact runpcl output.
title: runpcl can emit a spurious blank line, falsifying a byte-compare against perl
